title: Cooking & food safety
description: Useful basics for meals, storage, and outages.

cards.title: Cook with a thermometer
cards.summary: A food thermometer is more reliable than color or texture. Poultry and leftovers need 165°F (74°C); ground meats need 160°F (71°C).
steps: Check the thickest part with a clean food thermometer.
Cook chicken, turkey, and leftovers to 165°F (74°C).
Cook ground meats, including ground venison, to 160°F (71°C).
For whole cuts and fish, use the linked chart for the correct temperature and rest time.

cards.title: Decide what to keep after an outage
cards.summary: An unopened refrigerator usually keeps food cold about four hours; a full freezer about 48 hours, or 24 hours if half full. Temperature matters more than the clock.
steps: Keep appliance doors closed and note when power failed.
Check food with an appliance or food thermometer when power returns.
Discard perishable food above 40°F (4°C) for two hours or more.
Never taste food to decide whether it is safe.
cards.source: FoodSafety.gov food safety during a power outage

cards.title: Make a simple shelf-stable meal
cards.summary: Combine a grain, a protein, and vegetables from sealed shelf-stable packages. Use clean water and heat only where ventilation is safe.
steps: Choose rice or another grain, canned beans or fish, and canned vegetables.
Check packaging and dates; discard swollen, leaking, or badly damaged cans.
Wash hands and clean utensils with safe water.
Heat with equipment intended for that space; never use a camp stove or grill indoors.
cards.source: Ready.gov emergency kit; FoodSafety.gov disaster food safety
